name: Zoho CRM
verdict: Likely self-serve: register a Server-based client in the Zoho API Console, with no approval to connect. The catch is data centers, so send each customer to their own region's accounts server and api_domain; low confidence.
needGuide: Yes — data centers and per-user refresh-token limits trip people up, so follow a region-aware flow.

auth.detail: Likely: authorization-code flow at accounts.zoho.<dc>/oauth/v2/auth with access_type=offline for a refresh token. Access tokens last 1 hour; refresh tokens do not expire but a per-user cap applies (about 20 per client, oldest dropped) and access-token minting is rate-limited. Responses return location, accounts-server and api_domain for the customer's data center. Unverified this session.

effort.timeToProduction: 1–3 days (no review); Marketplace listing takes weeks (unverified)

approval.gate: No approval to connect: a Server-based client works for any Zoho CRM org. Enable the multi-data-center option so one client works across regions, then route each user to their own accounts and api_domain host. Zoho Marketplace publishing is separate, optional and reviewed.

scopes.why: Fine-grained module and operation scopes (for example ZohoCRM.modules.contacts.READ); no scope review for direct OAuth use.
scopes.summary: Granular scopes such as ZohoCRM.modules.ALL, ZohoCRM.modules.contacts.READ, ZohoCRM.settings.READ, ZohoCRM.users.READ, ZohoCRM.org.READ. No scope review applies to direct OAuth use; Marketplace review is separate.

cost: Free API console; Zoho CRM edition limits apply to customers' API credits
prerequisites: Account and owner: Any Zoho account holder can create clients; use a company-owned Zoho account, since clients are tied to the creating user.
Where you register: api-console.zoho.com (use the regional console for EU, IN, AU, JP, CA, SA, CN) → Add Client → Server-based Applications → set homepage and redirect URI, copy client ID and secret
Cost: Free API console; Zoho CRM edition limits apply to customers' API credits

registerAt.path: api-console.zoho.com (use the regional console for EU, IN, AU, JP, CA, SA, CN) → Add Client → Server-based Applications → set homepage and redirect URI, copy client ID and secret

steps.do: Create a company Zoho account and a test CRM org
Open api-console.zoho.com → Add Client → Server-based Applications; add redirect URI; tick use-same-credentials for all data centers
Build authorization URL per DC with scope ZohoCRM.modules.ALL (add others as needed), access_type=offline, prompt=consent
Exchange the code at the accounts-server value returned; save refresh token, api_domain and location
Call the CRM API at api_domain; refresh the access token hourly
Test with users in two data centers (for example com and eu)

roles.team: Any Zoho account holder can create clients; use a company-owned Zoho account, since clients are tied to the creating user.
roles.customer: A Zoho CRM user authorizes within their profile permissions; admins can limit API access and manage Connected Apps (likely). An admin is typically needed for org-wide scopes such as settings or users.

testing: Self Client in the API Console generates a short-lived grant token (about 10 minutes) for server-side testing.
Test data centers matter: create the test org in the same region you will call.
Zoho CRM trial or free edition for tests; sandbox needs higher editions (likely).

blockers.fix: A user's account lives in one region; use the accounts-server and api_domain returned, never hardcode zoho.com.

blockers.problem: Refresh-token cap per user per client
blockers.fix: Persist and reuse tokens instead of reauthorizing.

blockers.problem: Wrong client type (Self Client in production) fails

automation.agentCan: Write multi-DC OAuth code, token store and refresh logic, scope selection and test calls.
automation.humanMust: Create the client in API Console, and have the customer user or admin authorize.

uncertain: Not fetched this session (hourly fetch limit hit), so all Zoho details come from prior knowledge.
